rv.q: It does feel static at times, and the pace slows too much towards the end, but these are teething problems for a directorial hand that shows great thought and skill.
This is RSC territory, with all the characters and the backstage team pulling together to create a first-class experience for all.
It’s funny and touching, something Fiennes treads succinctly and beautifully.
Fiennes puts his own mark on the comedy – here’s to him turning his attention to another.
This As You Like It is a reminder that Shakespeare does not always need the director’s hand to steer.
What is wonderful and feels so fresh and exciting about this production are the three young central actresses playing Rosalind, Celicia and Phebe.
As a director of comedy he needs to find a lighter touch though.

cn.t: Fiennes' directorial debut favors somber stillness over comic fizz, but radiant performances from Walter, Obianyo, and James elevate this stripped-down production into a moving, precisely spoken take on Shakespeare's comedy.
